response: The legal criteria for third-party software include ensuring compliance with EU’s GDPR and considering the geo-location of services and their data privacy agreements, especially when third-party providers may need to be listed in virtualQ’s Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with clients. Licenses and intellectual property (IP) ownership are evaluated to confirm that open-source components can be appropriately integrated into virtualQ’s system, including for commercial use or in an exit scenario. Given the sensitivity of data from customers regulated under SGB and KRITIS, careful assessment is required for any party that could potentially access the data, even in theory.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits involve reviews and design verification conducted within the organization, such as architecture and design sessions, pull request reviews, and assessments using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which evaluates operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. These audits are carried out by internal teams like the Head of Engineering and engineers, with findings tracked as technical debt. External audits, on the other hand, involve third-party evaluations, including penetration testing and security assessments performed by external partners or through external tooling, focusing on both the codebase and non-production environments. The key difference lies in the internal versus external execution and validation of security and system integrity.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: Internal audits are conducted by the team through internal reviews, architecture and design sessions, and pull request reviews, focusing on verifying the virtualQ system and tracking technical debt. expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: VirtualQ offers two optimizers: the Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). The AFO is described on page 38, while the APO is detailed on page 39. Their specific functions and capabilities within the virtualQ system are outlined on these respective pages.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: The legal criteria require that any third‑party component comply with GDPR and related data‑privacy rules, that the provider’s geo‑location and data‑processing agreements can be listed in the DPAs virtualQ shares with its clients, and that the component’s license and IP ownership are “appropriate” for commercial use and for a possible exit sale of the virtualQ system. In addition, for customers governed by the German Social Code (SGB) or operating critical infrastructure (KRITIS), the software must satisfy the stricter requirements set out by the Federal Office for IT Security.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits are performed by the organization’s own teams – the Head of Engineering, engineers, and dedicated internal meetings – to review architecture, design, and data‑flow against the six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability). Findings are logged as technical debt and followed up according to criticality, with reviews happening once or twice a year. External audits, by contrast, use third‑party tooling or services to verify the virtualQ system (both code‑base and non‑production live environments) and include manual penetration‑testing performed by a partner, as well as AWS Well‑Architected Framework self‑service checks. Thus, internal audits rely on internal expertise and governance processes, whereas external audits bring independent, outside validation and specialized security testing.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

VirtualQ offers two distinct optimizer products:

* **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)** – an optimizer that automatically tunes and adjusts the system to provide flexible, rule‑based improvements across the platform. 【Context: “Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)”】  
* **Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)** – an optimizer that uses predictive analytics to anticipate workload patterns and automatically apply optimisations that improve performance and resource usage. 【Context: “Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)”】

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response: The legal criteria for third-party software include ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations such as the EU’s GDPR, particularly regarding the geo-location of services and potential data access by third parties. Special consideration is given to customers under strict regulations like SGB and KRITIS, requiring careful evaluation of data processing agreements (DPAs) with service providers. Additionally, licenses and intellectual property (IP) ownership are assessed to confirm that open source components can be commercially used and integrated into the virtualQ system without legal risk.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits involve reviews of the virtualQ system through team-led architecture and design sessions, pull request reviews, and assessments using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, focusing on areas like security and reliability. External audits are conducted by external partners using tooling or manual penetration testing on non-production systems to verify security and compliance. Internal audits are performed by internal teams like the Head of Engineering and engineers, while external audits rely on third-party partners. Findings from both types are tracked as technical debt and addressed based on criticality.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: virtualQ offers two optimizers: the Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). While the context does not provide detailed descriptions of their functions, their names suggest that AFO focuses on flexible automation and APO on predictive automation within the virtualQ system. expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: The legal criteria for 3rd party software include ensuring GDPR compliance, reviewing data privacy agreements, and examining licenses and IP ownership. These criteria are particularly important as they help avoid legal issues and ensure that we can derive proven value from the library or tool without facing lock-in or end-of-life (EoL) concerns.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits are conducted by engineers and reviewed in pull request evaluations, focusing on ensuring adherence to best practices and architectural guidelines. External audits, on the other hand, involve using external tooling and services to verify the virtualQ system in the code base or live system in a non-production stage, and are performed by a partner for tasks such as penetration testing.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: VirtualQ offers two optimizers: the 38 Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the 39 Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). These optimizers play a role in enhancing the system’s performance, with AFO likely focusing on flexibility and APO on predictive capabilities.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

The legal criteria focus on **data‑protection compliance and licensing**.  
- Because the system handles EU‑GDPR‑regulated data, any third‑party service must have appropriate **geo‑location, data‑privacy agreements and be listed in the DPAs that virtualQ shares with its clients** (see “Legal Criteria … GDPR, geo‑location of services and their data privacy agreements are being carefully considered”).  
- In addition, the **software’s license and IP ownership must permit commercial use and resale** (the “appropriate” test) and must satisfy the stricter requirements of regulated customers such as GDPR‑covered entities, Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB) clients, KRITIS operators, and the Federal Office of IT Security.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

Internal audits are performed by the organization’s own teams (e.g., the Head of Engineering, engineers, and architects) through internal reviews, architecture‑design sessions, and the regular “Internal Audits & Design Verification” process that checks the virtualQ system against six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability). They occur once or twice a year, and any findings are logged as technical debt and prioritized by criticality.  

External audits, by contrast, use third‑party tooling or services to evaluate the virtualQ code base or live (non‑production) system, and include manual security‑focused penetration testing carried out by an external partner, as described in the “External Audits” section. These audits verify compliance from an outside perspective rather than internal governance.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

VirtualQ provides two distinct optimizer products:

1. **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)** – a tool that applies flexible, rule‑based optimization to the virtualQ platform (see “Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)” in the document).  
2. **Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)** – a solution that uses predictive analytics/ML to anticipate workload patterns and automatically tune the system for optimal performance (see “Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)” in the document).  

Together, the AFO handles configurable, on‑the‑fly adjustments, while the APO leverages data‑driven forecasts to continuously optimize the service.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: The legal criteria for third-party software include ensuring compliance with GDPR and data privacy agreements, especially regarding the geo-location of services and potential access to regulated data. Licenses and IP ownership are evaluated to confirm that open-source components can be used commercially and integrated into the virtualQ system without legal risk. Services must also be considered for inclusion in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with clients, particularly when handling data subject to strict regulations like SGB or KRITIS.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits involve reviews of the virtualQ system through team-led architecture and design sessions, pull request reviews for smaller decisions, and audits using frameworks like the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which evaluates six pillars such as Security and Operational Excellence. These audits are conducted internally by the Head of Engineering and engineering teams, with findings tracked as technical debt. External audits, on the other hand, involve third-party partners performing manual security assessments like penetration testing and using external tools to verify the codebase or non-production environments. The key difference is that internal audits focus on design and operational best practices within the team, while external audits provide independent validation of security and system integrity.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: virtualQ offers two optimizers: the Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). While the context mentions these components, it does not provide specific details about their functions or differences.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: Internal audits are conducted by engineers and involve pull request reviews for smaller decisions, while larger strategic decisions or architectural guardrails are reviewed in dedicated internal meetings. External audits, on the other hand, rely on external tooling/services to verify the virtualQ system, either in the code base or in the live system during a non-production stage.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: VirtualQ offers two different optimizers: the Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: The legal criteria for adopting 3rd‑party software focus on data‑protection and licensing compliance. They require that the provider’s **geographic location, privacy agreements and GDPR obligations** (including any DPAs that virtualQ must share with its clients) be compatible with the regulated data that virtualQ handles, especially for GDPR, SGB‑regulated customers and KRITIS‑critical‑infrastructure users. In addition, the software’s **license and IP ownership** must be “appropriate” – i.e., allow commercial use and resale of the virtualQ system, including any exit‑scenario transfers. These checks ensure that no party can (even theoretically) gain unauthorized access to the data while meeting all regulatory and contractual requirements.

Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
Internal audits are carried out by the organisation’s own teams (e.g., Head of Engineering, engineers reviewing pull‑requests and holding internal architecture/design meetings) and focus on the six WA‑Framework pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability). Findings are recorded as technical debt and tracked for remediation according to their criticality, typically once or twice a year.  

External audits are performed by third‑party services or partners; they use external tooling to verify the virtualQ system in the code base or a non‑production live environment and include manual security‑related penetration testing. They also leverage frameworks such as the AWS Well‑Architected self‑service audit, providing an independent assessment of compliance and best‑practice adherence.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response:
VirtualQ ships two built‑in AI‑driven optimizers:

* **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)** – an automated engine that applies flexible, rule‑based optimisation to the virtualQ platform (see “Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)” in the document).  
* **Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)** – an automated engine that uses predictive models and training data to optimise outcomes in the system (see “Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)” in the document).

Together they form the AI/ML‑based optimisation layer of the virtualQ system.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response: The legal criteria for 3rd party software include ensuring compliance with GDPR, especially regarding the geo-location of services and data privacy agreements, as virtualQ handles data regulated by the EU’s GDPR and other strict frameworks like SGB and KRITIS. Licenses and IP ownership are carefully evaluated to confirm that open source components can be appropriately integrated into the virtualQ system, including use in commercial settings or during an exit scenario. Services must also be assessable for inclusion in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) shared with clients, particularly when third-party providers may access sensitive data.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits involve reviews and design verification conducted within the organization, such as architecture and design sessions, pull request reviews, and assessments using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which evaluates six pillars like security and reliability. External audits are performed by third parties using external tools or services to verify the virtualQ system’s codebase or non-production environments, and include manual security assessments like penetration testing by a partner. The key difference is that internal audits are organization-led and focus on design and operational processes, while external audits are independent evaluations focused on security and system integrity.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: virtualQ offers two optimizers: the Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). While the context does not provide detailed descriptions of their functions, their names suggest that AFO focuses on flexibility in optimization processes, and APO leverages predictive capabilities, likely using AI/ML techniques. expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response: Internal audits involve reviews and architecture sessions within the team, focusing on verifying the virtualQ system in the code base or live system, while external audits are conducted using external tooling/services to verify the virtualQ system. Internal audits are often part of smaller decision processes and pull request reviews, whereas external audits utilize AWS Well Architected Framework and are carried out once or twice a year.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: VirtualQ offers two optimizers: the Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO) and the Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO). The AFO and APO help streamline and improve the performance and predictive capabilities of the system.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response: The legal criteria focus on **data‑protection compliance and licensing suitability**.  Any 3rd‑party component must respect the EU GDPR (including geo‑location of the service and privacy agreements that may need to be listed in the DPAs shared with virtualQ’s clients) and meet the stricter requirements of regulated customers such as those under the Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB) or KRITIS, which are governed by the Federal Office of IT Security.  In addition, the software’s **license and IP ownership** must allow commercial use and potential resale of the virtualQ system (i.e., be “appropriate” for a commercial/exits scenario).  These criteria are evaluated before the library or tool is integrated.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

Internal audits are performed by the organization’s own teams (e.g., Head of Engineering, engineers) through internal reviews, architecture‑design sessions and pull‑request checks; they are tracked as technical debt and follow the six‑pillar framework (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability) 【Context】.  

External audits are carried out by third‑party services or partners – using external tooling to verify the virtualQ code base or non‑production live system and conducting manual security tests such as penetration testing – and also include self‑service checks like the AWS Well‑Architected Framework 【Context】.  

The key difference is that internal audits rely on internal staff and processes to monitor adherence to best practices, while external audits use independent tools or external experts to provide an outside verification of security, compliance and architectural soundness.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response: VirtualQ provides two AI‑driven optimizers – the **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)** and the **Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)** (see the “Optimizers” section of the document). The AFO continuously and automatically fine‑tunes system settings in a flexible, rule‑based way, while the APO leverages predictive models and training data to anticipate future demand and automatically adjust resources for optimal performance【38‑AFO】【39‑APO】.
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response:
Great question! When it comes to using third-party software or services at virtualQ, we take legal criteria very seriously—especially because we handle sensitive data protected by strict rules like the EU’s GDPR and other high-standard regulations (like those for KRITIS or social code/SGB customers).

Here’s what we look at before bringing in any third-party tool or library:

1. **Data Privacy & Location**: We make sure the service respects data privacy and that any data processing happens in compliance with GDPR. This includes checking *where* the data is stored and processed—because location matters under EU law.

2. **Data Processing Agreements (DPAs)**: If a third-party service handles personal data, they may need to be listed in our DPAs with clients. So we check whether the provider can sign such agreements—this is a must.

3. **Licenses & IP Ownership**: For open-source tools or commercial software, we review the license carefully. We need to be sure we’re allowed to use, modify, and even sell the software as part of our system—especially if there’s ever an acquisition or exit.

4. **No Legal Risks**: We want to avoid any surprises down the road—like unexpected costs, legal claims, or restrictions on how we use the software.

In short: we only bring in third-party tools if they’re legally safe, privacy-compliant, and won’t put us (or our customers) at risk. It’s all about trust, control, and long-term stability.

Let me know if you'd like examples of how this works in practice! 😊
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
The central frameworks used in VirtualQ are **Ruby on Rails** and another one (the name of the second isn't clearly mentioned in the text you shared). 

The main one we know about is **Ruby on Rails** — it's a framework built with Ruby that helps developers build web applications quickly. It follows the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern, which organizes code in a clean, structured way. This framework is great for apps that need to exchange data with users (through websites or APIs), process that data, and store it in a database.

Think of a framework like a skeleton or blueprint for an app — it sets the structure and rules, so you don’t have to build everything from scratch. Unlike libraries (which are like handy tools you can swap out easily), switching frameworks usually takes a lot of work because they shape the entire app.

So, VirtualQ relies heavily on **Ruby on Rails** as one of its central frameworks to keep things running smoothly and consistently.

response:
Great question! Let me break it down in a simple way.

**Internal audits** are checks that your own team does to make sure everything is built correctly and securely. At virtualQ, these happen regularly and involve things like:

- Team discussions about system design and architecture.
- Reviewing code changes (like during pull requests) to catch issues early.
- Using the **AWS Well-Architected Framework**, which is a kind of self-check for cloud systems. It looks at six key areas—like security, reliability, and performance—and shows where improvements can be made. These checks are done once or twice a year, and any issues found are tracked and fixed based on how serious they are.

The main people involved are usually the **Head of Engineering** and the engineering team.

On the other hand, **external audits** are done by people outside the company—like security experts or third-party services. They give an objective, outside view of the system. These include:

- Automated checks using external tools to scan the code or test the system in a safe (non-production) environment.
- Manual security tests, like **penetration testing**, where a partner tries to find and report vulnerabilities, just like a hacker might.

So, the big difference is:
- **Internal audits** = your own team checking your work.
- **External audits** = independent experts double-checking for security and quality.

Both are important—they help catch different kinds of issues and make sure the system stays safe, reliable, and well-built.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

response:
Great question! 😊

virtualQ offers two main optimizers:

1. **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)**  
2. **Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)**

Here's what they do in simple terms:

- The **AFO (Automated Flexible Optimizer)** helps the system adapt quickly to different needs or changes. Think of it like a smart assistant that adjusts settings on the fly to keep things running smoothly, no matter how the workload or environment changes.

- The **APO (Automated Predictive Optimizer)** is more like a forward-thinker. It uses patterns and data (this is where AI/ML comes in) to *predict* what might happen next and optimizes the system ahead of time. For example, if it sees usage going up every Monday morning, it can prep the system before the rush hits.

Together, these optimizers help virtualQ stay fast, efficient, and ready for whatever comes its way—whether it's changing demands or growing workloads. Pretty cool, right? 🚀
expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response:
Hey there! Based on what you've shared, the legal criteria for using 3rd party software are pretty important because we're dealing with data that has to meet strict regulations. Here’s the breakdown in simple terms:

1. **Data Privacy**: Since we're working with data that's regulated by the EU’s GDPR, we need to make sure that any 3rd party software or service we use adheres to these data privacy laws. This means we have to check if the software complies with GDPR and whether it’s located in a place where the data protection laws are robust.

2. **Data Privacy Agreements**: When using 3rd party services, we need to ensure that there are proper data privacy agreements in place. If these services are run by other companies, they must be listed in Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) that we share with our clients.

3. **Licenses and IP Ownership**: It’s super important that the licenses for any software or tools we use are clear. This is especially true for open-source components. We also need to know who owns the intellectual property (IP) to avoid any future legal issues.

4. **Regulatory Compliance**: Depending on who our customers are—like those regulated under the German social code (Sozialgesetzbuch, SGB) or running critical infrastructure (KRITIS)—we might have additional legal requirements. These go beyond what the Federal Office of IT Security (Bundesamt für Sicherheit) defines.

So, in short, our legal criteria for 3rd party software focus on making sure we’re complying with data privacy laws, have solid agreements in place, and understand who owns the software and its IP. Hope this helps! If you have more questions, feel free to ask. 😊
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

Sure thing! So, the central frameworks are like the backbone of a software project. They help structure and guide how the entire application is built, managed, and maintained. 

In our case, we're using two main frameworks:

1. **Ruby on Rails**:
   - It's a model-view-controller (MVC) framework written in Ruby.
   - Its main job is to simplify and speed up the process of creating applications that interact with clients through user interfaces (UIs) or APIs.
   - It handles tasks like exchanging data with clients, processing data, and storing it in a database.

2. **Elixir** (with Phoenix framework):
   - It works alongside Ruby on Rails for certain parts of the application.
   - It's used for application logic, similar to how Ruby on Rails handles other parts.

In simpler terms, these frameworks provide the structure and rules for building and organizing the software. They make it easier for developers to work together and maintain the code over time. So, if you need to switch out some parts that do specific tasks (like logging or monitoring), you can do that relatively easily. But changing the overall framework would be much harder because it would affect how everything is set up.
