Internal audits:
Internal audits refer to reviews and verification processes conducted within the organization to assess the virtualQ system. These include architecture and design sessions within the team, pull request reviews for smaller decisions, and dedicated internal meetings for larger or strategic decisions and architectural guardrails. Additionally, the AWS Well-Architected Framework is used as a self-service audit tool for systems running on cloud or hybrid setups. This audit evaluates six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, and Sustainability. It is conducted once or twice a year, with findings tracked as technical debt and addressed based on criticality. Participants in internal audits include the Head of Engineering and other team members.

External audits:
External audits involve assessments performed by external parties or tools. These include audits based on external tooling or services that verify the virtualQ system either in the codebase or in a non-production environment. Additionally, manual security-related audits such as penetration testing are carried out by a partner. These audits focus specifically on security aspects of the system.

Key differences:
- Internal audits are conducted by internal teams and processes (e.g., design sessions, pull requests, self-service AWS audits), while external audits are performed by external partners or tools.
- Internal audits cover broader operational and architectural aspects across six pillars, whereas external audits are primarily focused on security verification and penetration testing.
- Internal audits occur on a scheduled basis (once or twice a year for the AWS audit), while the frequency of external audits is not specified but involves ongoing verification via external services.

Not enough information in the provided documents to determine:
- The exact frequency of external audits beyond the mention of penetration testing by a partner.
- Whether all external audits are security-focused or if some cover other domains.
- Detailed methodology or scope of the external partner’s penetration testing.
- The specific roles of the Chief Executive Officer and external security advisor in either audit type beyond their listed participation.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

   - Licenses and intellectual property (IP) ownership are evaluated, especially for open-source components.
   - Licenses must be appropriate for commercial use and for potential sale of the virtualQ system in an exit scenario.

2. **How These Pieces Connect**:
   - The legal criteria are driven by compliance with strict data protection laws (GDPR, SGB, KRITIS) and the need to maintain trust and contractual obligations with clients.
   - Any third-party software or service that processes personal or sensitive data must support compliance through mechanisms like DPAs and appropriate data handling practices.
   - The licensing terms of third-party software (especially open source) must allow integration into a commercial product without creating IP conflicts or restrictions on distribution or sale.

3. **Conclusion**:
   The legal criteria for third-party software include:
   - Compliance with GDPR and other relevant regulations (e.g., SGB, KRITIS).
   - Data privacy considerations, including the geographic location of data processing.
   - The ability to include the third party in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) if they process personal data.
   - Evaluation of software licenses to ensure they permit commercial use and integration into virtualQ’s system.
   - Ensuring licenses do not restrict future sale or distribution of virtualQ, especially in an exit scenario.
   - Proper assessment of IP ownership to avoid legal conflicts.

**Final Answer**:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software are: compliance with GDPR, SGB, and KRITIS regulations; appropriate data privacy practices including geographic data handling; inclusion in DPAs when applicable; use of licenses that permit commercial integration and future sale of the system; and clear intellectual property rights to avoid legal risks.

1. **Relevant Information from the Context:**

   - **Internal Audits & Design Verification** are conducted through:
     - Regular code reviews.
     - Internal architecture and design sessions within the team.
     - Smaller decisions made and verified by engineers via pull request reviews.
     - Larger strategic or architectural decisions made in dedicated internal meetings.
     - Use of the **AWS Well-Architected Framework**, a self-service audit tool focusing on six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability).
     - Conducted once or twice a year, with findings tracked as technical debt and followed up based on criticality.
     - Participants include the **Head of Engineering** and internal teams.

   - **External Audits** involve:
     - Use of external tooling or services to verify the virtualQ system, either in the codebase or in a non-production environment.
     - Manual security-related audits such as **penetration testing** carried out by a partner.
     - Also based on verification of the system by external entities.
     - Implied participants include an **external security advisor** and third-party partners.

2. **How These Pieces Connect:**

   - Both internal and external audits aim to verify the security, reliability, and best practices of the **virtualQ system**.
   - Internal audits are **proactive, process-driven, and self-conducted**, focusing on design, architecture, and cloud best practices using frameworks like AWS Well-Architected.
   - External audits are **independent validations** from outside parties, providing objective assessments—especially in security (e.g., penetration testing) and code/system integrity.
   - The two types of audits complement each other: internal audits ensure ongoing adherence to standards, while external audits provide third-party verification and identify blind spots.

3. **Conclusion:**

   Internal audits are **organization-led reviews** involving internal teams and tools to evaluate system design, architecture, and operational practices, often using standardized frameworks. External audits are **independent evaluations** performed by third parties using specialized tools or manual testing (like penetration tests) to validate security and system integrity. The key difference lies in **who performs the audit** (internal team vs. external partner) and the **nature of assessment** (process and design-focused vs. independent, security-focused validation).

---

**Final Answer:**

Internal audits are assessments conducted by the organization’s own team (e.g., engineers, Head of Engineering) using internal processes such as code reviews, design sessions, and self-service tools like the AWS Well-Architected Framework. They focus on evaluating system design, architecture, and adherence to best practices across areas like security, reliability, and cost efficiency. These are typically performed periodically (once or twice a year) and findings are managed as technical debt.

External audits, in contrast, are performed by third-party partners or external tools and involve objective verification of the system—either in code or in a non-production environment. These include security-focused activities like penetration testing and are used to validate the system’s security and integrity independently.

The key difference is that **internal audits are self-assessments focused on design and operations**, while **external audits are independent evaluations emphasizing security and compliance through external validation**.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.

Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

**Legal criteria for using 3rd‑party software (or services)** | # | Criterion | What it means / what must be checked | |---|-----------|----------------------------------------| | 1 | **GDPR compliance** | The library / service must respect EU‑wide data‑protection rules (lawful basis, data‑subject rights, breach‑notification, etc.). | | 2 | **Geographical location of processing** | Verify where the provider’s infrastructure (cloud, data‑centres) is located and that the location is allowed under the GDPR and any contractual DPA requirements. | | 3 | **Data‑privacy agreements / DPA inclusion** | The provider must be able to be listed in the Data‑Processing Agreements (DPAs) that *virtualQ* signs with its clients, and must sign appropriate data‑processing addenda. | | 4 | **Licensing model & IP ownership** | • Identify the exact license (e.g., MIT, Apache 2.0, GPL‑3, proprietary).
• Confirm that the license permits the intended commercial use, redistribution, and inclusion in a product that may be sold or transferred in an exit scenario.
• Ensure there are no conflicting IP claims (patents, trademarks) that could affect *virtualQ*. | | 5 | **“Appropriate” for commercial/exitable use** | The license must be **commercial‑friendly** (i.e., not “non‑commercial only”) and must allow the component to be sold together with *virtualQ* or transferred to a buyer in a future exit. | | 6 | **Sector‑specific regulatory fit** | For customers subject to:
• **GDPR** (general EU data‑protection)
• **Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB)** – social‑law regulations
• **KRITIS** – critical‑infrastructure obligations
the software must meet the stricter standards defined by the **Federal Office for Information Security (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik – BSI)**, which often go beyond baseline GDPR. | | 7 | **Vendor lock‑in / End‑of‑Life (EoL) risk** | Although primarily an operational risk, the legal side requires that the license does not create a proprietary lock‑in that would prevent future migration or maintenance without breaching contract terms. | | 8 | **Third‑party liability & warranty** | Check that the provider offers warranty/indemnity clauses for IP infringement, security vulnerabilities, and compliance failures. | | 9 | **Export‑control & sanctions** | Ensure the software (or its underlying technology) is not subject to export restrictions or sanctions that would prohibit its use with EU customers. | |10| **Audit & traceability rights** | The contract should grant *virtualQ* the right to audit the provider’s compliance (e.g., proof of GDPR‑compliant data handling, security certifications). | ### How the criteria are derived from the context 1. **GDPR & data‑privacy** – explicitly mentioned as a core concern for any 3rd‑party service. 2. **Geo‑location & DPAs** – the text stresses that services must be listed in the DPAs *virtualQ* shares with its clients. 3. **Licenses & IP ownership** – the document notes that “licenses are crucial when it comes to integrating open‑source components” and that they must be “appropriate” for commercial use or an exit scenario. 4. **Sector‑specific rules** – customers regulated under GDPR, the German Social Code (SGB), and KRITIS have requirements that exceed the baseline BSI guidelines. 5. **Commercial‑appropriateness** – the word “appropriate” is defined as “whether it can be used in a commercial setting or can be sold along with the virtualQ system in an exit scenario.” 6. **Lock‑in / EoL** – mentioned as an operational risk, but it also has a legal dimension (contractual obligations, future migration rights). ### Bottom line When evaluating any third‑party software or service, *virtualQ* must verify that it: 1. **Respects GDPR and any sector‑specific data‑protection rules**, 2. **Operates from an approved geographic location and can be covered by a DPA**, 3. **Is provided under a license that permits commercial use, redistribution, and exit‑scenario transfer**, 4. **Has clear IP ownership and includes indemnities for infringement**, 5. **Meets the higher standards required for SGB and KRITIS customers**, and 6. **Does not create legal lock‑in, export‑control, or audit‑ability problems**. Only if all of these legal criteria are satisfied should the library or tool be approved for integration into the *virtualQ* system.

response:
**Step‑by‑step reasoning**

1. **Identify the pieces of information that describe the two audit types**

   * **Internal audits** (described in the “Internal Audits & Design Verification” section)  
     - Performed by the **Head of Engineering**, engineers, and internal review bodies.  
     - Conducted through **architecture & design sessions**, **pull‑request reviews**, and **dedicated internal meetings**.  
     - Evaluated against six pillars: **Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability**.  
     - Results are recorded as **technical‑debt items** and tracked by **criticality**.  
     - Frequency: **once or twice a year** (or more often for day‑to‑day PR reviews).  

   * **External audits** (described in the “External Audits” section)  
     - Performed by **outside parties or tools**: an **external security advisor**, a **partner that runs penetration‑testing**, and **AWS Well‑Architected Framework** self‑service audits.  
     - Use **external tooling/services** to verify the **virtualQ system** (code‑base or live non‑production environment).  
     - Include **manual security‑related audits** (e.g., pen‑testing) and **cloud‑infrastructure reviews**.  
     - Provide an **independent, third‑party view** of compliance and security posture.

2. **Connect the information**

   - Both audit types aim to assess the same six pillars, but **who performs the assessment** and **how** it is done differ.  
   - Internal audits are **owner‑driven**, embedded in the development workflow, and feed directly into the team’s backlog as technical‑debt items.  
   - External audits are **independent**, often mandated by regulations (e.g., NIS2, SGB) or best‑practice frameworks, and rely on **outside expertise and tooling** to validate the system from an outsider’s perspective.

3. **Derive the differences**

   | Aspect | Internal Audit | External Audit |
   |--------|----------------|----------------|
   | **Performed by** | Internal team (Head of Engineering, engineers, internal reviewers) | Third‑party entities (external security advisor, penetration‑testing partner, AWS Well‑Architected service) |
   | **Scope & Tools** | Architecture/design reviews, PR reviews, internal meetings; uses internal knowledge and processes | External tooling/services, manual penetration testing, cloud‑framework checks |
   | **Perspective** | Owner’s view – focuses on improving day‑to‑day operations and tracking technical debt | Independent/objective view – validates compliance, security, and best‑practice adherence |
   | **Frequency** | Typically 1–2 times per year (plus continuous PR checks) | Usually aligned with contractual or regulatory cycles; can be ad‑hoc or scheduled by the external provider |
   | **Outcome handling** | Findings become internal technical‑debt items, prioritized by criticality within the team | Findings are reported back to the organization, often with formal remediation recommendations and may be required for regulatory compliance |
   | **Regulatory role** | Supports internal governance and continuous improvement | Provides evidence for external compliance (e.g., NIS2, SGB) and third‑party assurance |

**Conclusion**

- **Internal audits** are **in‑house evaluations** carried out by the organization’s own engineers and leadership to ensure that the system follows internal standards and to capture improvement work as technical debt.  
- **External audits** are **independent assessments** performed by outside specialists or automated services that verify the system against external standards, regulations, and best‑practice frameworks.  

The key differences lie in **who conducts the audit, the tools and perspective used, how findings are managed, and the role each audit plays in compliance versus continuous internal improvement**.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response:
1. **Relevant Information from the Context:**
   - The use of third-party software and services requires careful evaluation before integration.
   - Legal criteria are especially important due to the nature of the data handled: regulated by **EU’s GDPR**, **social code (SGB)**, and **critical infrastructure (KRITIS)**.
   - **Data privacy agreements** must be considered, particularly for services run by third-party providers, as these may need to be included in **Data Processing Agreements (DPAs)** between virtualQ and its clients.
   - **Geo-location of services** is a key concern — where data is processed or stored impacts compliance.
   - **Licenses and IP ownership** are evaluated, especially for open-source components.
   - Not all open-source licenses are suitable — only those that allow commercial use and integration into the virtualQ system, including in an **exit scenario** (e.g., resale or transfer of the system).
   - The term “**appropriate**” in licensing refers to whether the software can be used commercially or sold with the virtualQ system.

2. **How These Pieces Connect:**
   - The legal criteria are driven by compliance obligations (GDPR, SGB, KRITIS), which impose strict requirements on data handling and processor accountability.
   - Because virtualQ shares DPAs with clients, any third-party service that processes personal data must be compliant and potentially listed in those DPAs.
   - The geographic location of data processing affects whether data transfers are lawful under GDPR (e.g., transfers outside the EU require safeguards).
   - Open-source licenses must not restrict commercial use or create IP conflicts, especially in future scenarios like company sale or product licensing.

3. **Conclusion:**
   The legal criteria for third-party software and services include:
   - Compliance with **GDPR**, **SGB**, and **KRITIS** regulations.
   - **Data privacy and processing agreements** (e.g., DPAs) must cover the third party if they process personal data.
   - **Geo-location of data processing/storage** must meet EU data residency and transfer requirements.
   - **Software licenses** must permit commercial use and integration into virtualQ’s offerings, including in exit scenarios (no restrictive open-source licenses like AGPL unless approved).
   - Clear **IP ownership** and no legal risk from license incompatibility or viral licensing terms.

**Final Answer:**
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include: (1) compliance with GDPR, SGB, and KRITIS regulations; (2) inclusion in or compatibility with Data Processing Agreements (DPAs); (3) acceptable geo-location of data processing to ensure lawful data transfers under EU law; (4) use of commercially permissible licenses that allow integration and resale of the virtualQ system; and (5) clear intellectual property ownership and absence of restrictive or incompatible open-source license terms.

Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

1. **Relevant Information from the Context:**

- **Internal Audits & Design Verification** are conducted through internal reviews, architecture and design sessions within the team, and pull request reviews. Smaller technical decisions are verified during pull requests, while larger or strategic decisions (e.g., architectural guardrails) are made in dedicated internal meetings or audits.

- The **AWS Well-Architected Framework** is mentioned as a self-service audit tool for cloud or hybrid setups. It evaluates systems across six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, and Sustainability. This audit is conducted once or twice a year, findings are treated as technical debt, and follow-up actions are prioritized by criticality. Participants include the Head of Engineering and the Chief Executive Officer.

- **External Audits** involve external tooling or services that verify the virtualQ system either in the codebase or in a non-production environment. Additionally, manual security audits such as **penetration testing** are carried out by an external partner.

- External audits focus on both automated verification (via tools) and manual security assessments by third parties.

2. **How These Pieces Connect:**

- Both internal and external audits aim to ensure system quality, security, and compliance with best practices, but they differ in **who conducts them** and **how**.

- **Internal audits** are team-led processes involving design discussions, code reviews, and structured internal assessments (e.g., using AWS’s framework), involving internal roles like the Head of Engineering and CEO.

- **External audits** rely on third-party tools or services and external partners to validate the system independently, especially for security (e.g., penetration testing), adding an objective, outside perspective.

- The AWS Well-Architected Framework, while self-service, appears to be treated as part of the internal audit process since it's conducted by internal participants and integrated into technical debt tracking.

3. **Conclusion:**

Internal audits are processes led by the organization’s own team—through design sessions, code reviews, and structured self-assessments—to evaluate architecture, design, and operational practices. External audits involve independent third parties using tools or manual methods (like penetration testing) to verify the security and integrity of the system, providing an objective evaluation.

---

**Final Answer:**

Internal audits are assessments conducted by the organization’s own team, including design reviews, architecture sessions, and self-evaluations (e.g., using the AWS Well-Architected Framework), focusing on best practices across operational, security, and performance domains. They are used to evaluate both technical decisions and strategic architecture, with findings tracked as technical debt.

External audits involve independent verification of the virtualQ system by third-party tools or security partners, including codebase analysis and manual penetration testing in non-production environments. These provide objective, external validation of the system’s security and compliance.

The key difference lies in the **actor** (internal team vs. external parties) and the **nature** of assessment: internal audits focus on continuous design and operational improvement, while external audits emphasize independent security and system validation.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung:

In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

**Legal criteria for using 3rd‑party software (as outlined in the document)** | # | Criterion | What it means / what must be verified | |---|-----------|----------------------------------------| | 1 | **GDPR compliance** | The library / service must respect the EU General Data Protection Regulation – lawful processing, data‑subject rights, breach‑notification, etc. | | 2 | **Data‑location / geo‑restriction** | The physical location of the service (or where data is stored/processed) must satisfy any residency requirements of the customer or the virtualQ DPA. | | 3 | **Data‑processing agreements (DPAs)** | The 3rd‑party must be able to be listed in the DPAs that virtualQ shares with its clients, and a DPA (or equivalent contract) must be in place that governs how the provider handles personal data. | | 4 | **Licensing compatibility** | - The open‑source or commercial license must allow the intended use (integration, modification, redistribution).
- It must be “appropriate” – i.e., permissible for commercial exploitation and for inclusion in an exit‑sale of the virtualQ system. | | 5 | **Intellectual‑property (IP) ownership** | Verify who owns the code / assets and that no third‑party IP rights are infringed by using the component. | | 6 | **Regulatory‑specific requirements** | For customers subject to additional rules (e.g., German Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), KRITIS, or BSI‑defined security standards), the component must meet those higher security / privacy expectations. | | 7 | **Vendor lock‑in / End‑of‑Life (EoL) risk** | The legal terms must not create a lock‑in situation or expose virtualQ to an abrupt loss of support (e.g., short licence term, no maintenance clause). | | 8 | **Commercial‑use / exit‑scenario suitability** | The component must be allowed to be sold or transferred together with the virtualQ product in a future exit or acquisition (“appropriate” for commercial setting). | **In short:** Before adopting any 3rd‑party library or service, virtualQ checks that it complies with GDPR and any extra national/regional data‑privacy rules, that the data‑processing location and contracts (DPAs) are acceptable, that the software’s licence and IP rights allow the intended commercial use and future transfer, and that the component satisfies the stricter security/privacy demands of regulated customers (SGB, KRITIS, BSI). It also ensures there is no undue lock‑in or EoL risk.

### 1. Relevant information from the context | Source | What it tells us about the audit | |--------|---------------------------------| | **External audits** | • Performed with **external tooling/services** that check the *virtualQ* system – either the **code base** or the **live system** (in a non‑production stage).
• Include **manual security‑related audits** (penetration testing) carried out by a **partner**.
• Use third‑party frameworks such as the **AWS Well‑Architected Framework** (self‑service audit of cloud/hybrid assets). | | **Internal audits** | • Conducted **by the organization itself** (Head of Engineering, engineers, internal meetings).
• Combine **internal and external reviews**, architecture & design sessions, and “design verification”.
• Follow a **six‑pillar model** (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability).
• Identify divergences from best practice, log them as **technical debt**, and track remediation by criticality.
• Usually happen **once or twice a year**. | | **Participants & decision‑making** | • Small decisions → engineers (reviewed in PRs).
• Large/strategic decisions → internal meetings or audits, with Head of Engineering. | | **Purpose of both** | • Verify that the system meets **security, reliability, performance, cost, and sustainability** goals.
• Provide a basis for continuous improvement. | ### 2. How the pieces connect - Both audit types share the **same high‑level objectives** (checking the six pillars, finding gaps, and driving remediation). - The **key distinction** lies in **who performs the audit and what tools/methods are used**: - **Internal audits** are **owned and executed by the company’s own teams** using internal processes (design reviews, architecture sessions, pull‑request checks). - **External audits** are **independent** – they rely on **third‑party tools, services, or partners** (e.g., external code‑analysis platforms, penetration‑testing firms, AWS Well‑Architected self‑service review). ### 3. Conclusion – Definition and differences #### **Internal Audits** - **Who:** Conducted by the organization’s own staff (Head of Engineering, engineers, internal review committees). - **How:** Through internal design/architecture reviews, pull‑request checks, dedicated audit meetings, and the six‑pillar assessment framework. - **What is examined:** Implementation against internal best‑practice guardrails, technical debt, process adherence, and overall alignment with the company’s strategic goals. - **Outcome:** Findings are logged as technical debt, prioritized by criticality, and tracked for remediation by the same teams that own the code. #### **External Audits** - **Who:** Performed by **independent third parties** – external tooling/services, security partners, or cloud‑provider frameworks (e.g., AWS Well‑Architected). - **How:** Automated scans of the code base or live (non‑production) environment, manual penetration testing, and compliance checks using external standards. - **What is examined:** Objective verification of security, reliability, performance, cost‑optimisation, and compliance from an **outside perspective**; often focuses on areas that internal teams may overlook or that require certification. - **Outcome:** Independent reports that highlight gaps, provide recommendations, and may be required for regulatory or contractual compliance. #### **Key Differences** | Aspect | Internal Audit | External Audit | |--------|----------------|----------------| | **Performed by** | In‑house team (engineers, Head of Engineering) | Third‑party tools, security partners, cloud provider frameworks | | **Primary focus** | Alignment with internal guardrails, technical debt, process improvement | Independent verification, compliance, security hardening, unbiased assessment | | **Methodology** | Architecture/design sessions, PR reviews, internal metrics | Automated external scans, penetration testing, self‑service cloud audits | | **Objectivity** | Subject to internal biases; deep knowledge of system | Higher objectivity; external perspective | | **Regulatory role** | Mostly internal governance | Often required for external compliance, certifications, or stakeholder assurance | | **Frequency** | Typically 1–2 times per year (or as part of continuous internal review) | Typically 1–2 times per year, but may be triggered by contracts or regulatory deadlines | --- **In short:** - **Internal audits** are the organization’s own systematic checks of design, implementation, and process against its own best‑practice pillars, feeding directly into internal remediation cycles. - **External audits** are independent assessments using third‑party tools or partners that validate the system from an outside viewpoint, often with a stronger emphasis on security, compliance, and unbiased verification. Both complement each other to ensure the virtualQ system meets operational, security, and sustainability goals.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

**How the answer was derived**

2. **Connecting the pieces**

   - The adjective *Predictive* together with the mention of AI/ML points to an optimizer that uses forecasts to set parameters before the demand materialises.

3. **Conclusion**

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

**Legal criteria for using 3rd‑party software (as described in the context)** | # | Criterion | What it means in practice | Why it matters | |---|-----------|---------------------------|----------------| | 1 | **GDPR compliance** | – The library / service must support all GDPR obligations (lawful basis, data‑subject rights, breach‑notification, data‑minimisation, etc.).
– Any personal data it processes must stay within the legal framework (e.g., Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers outside the EU). | VirtualQ handles EU‑regulated data; a breach would create legal liability and could break contracts with customers. | | 2 | **Geo‑location / data‑residency** | – The provider’s data‑centres must be located in jurisdictions approved by the customer (usually EU/EEA).
– If the service stores or processes data elsewhere, a lawful transfer mechanism must be in place. | Many customers (especially public‑sector or critical‑infrastructure) require that data never leave the EU. | | 3 | **Inclusion in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs)** | – The 3rd‑party must be listed as a sub‑processor in the DPA that VirtualQ signs with its clients.
– The DPA must contain the required clauses (security, audit rights, breach notification, etc.). | DPAs are contractual evidence that all processing parties meet the client’s compliance obligations. | | 4 | **License suitability (“Appropriate” use)** | – The software’s licence must permit commercial use, redistribution and, if needed, resale as part of VirtualQ’s product.
– No “viral” or copyleft conditions that would force VirtualQ to disclose its own proprietary code, unless that is acceptable. | Enables VirtualQ to sell the solution and to exit (sell the business) without licence‑related blockers. | | 5 | **IP ownership & rights** | – VirtualQ must have a clear, royalty‑free right to use, modify and distribute the code.
– No hidden patents or third‑party claims that could be asserted later. | Protects against infringement claims and ensures the product can be shipped to customers. | | 6 | **Sector‑specific regulatory fit** | – For customers subject to Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), KRITIS or the German Federal Office for IT Security (BSI) guidelines, the software must meet those higher‑than‑GDPR standards (e.g., stricter encryption, auditability, certified components). | Failure to meet these extra requirements would disqualify the component for those customers. | | 7 | **No lock‑in / end‑of‑life risk** | – The provider should have a clear roadmap, support commitments, and an exit path (source code availability or alternative).
– The component must not be discontinued in a way that forces a non‑compliant replacement. | Guarantees continuity of compliance and avoids a situation where VirtualQ is forced to use a non‑legal alternative. | ### How the pieces fit together 1. **Data protection** (GDPR, geo‑location, DPAs) ensures that any personal or regulated data handled by the 3rd‑party stays within the legal bounds required by both EU law and VirtualQ’s customers. 2. **Licensing & IP** guarantees that VirtualQ can legally incorporate, commercialise and later sell or transfer the software without violating copyright or licence terms. 3. **Sector‑specific rules** (SGB, KRITIS, BSI) add an extra layer for high‑sensitivity customers, meaning the chosen component must satisfy those stricter controls. 4. **Operational safeguards** (no lock‑in, clear EoL policy) protect the business from future legal or compliance problems caused by a discontinued or unsupported component. ### Bottom‑line answer The legal criteria for adopting a 3rd‑party software component are: 1. **Full GDPR compliance** (including lawful processing and data‑transfer mechanisms). 2. **Approved geo‑location / data‑residency** of the service. 3. **Explicit inclusion as a sub‑processor in the relevant DPAs**. 4. **A licence that is “appropriate” for commercial use and for any exit‑sale scenario** (no prohibitive copyleft, royalty‑free rights). 5. **Clear IP ownership and freedom from hidden patent or copyright claims**. 6. **Alignment with any sector‑specific regulations** (e.g., SGB, KRITIS, BSI). 7. **No lock‑in or unmanaged end‑of‑life risk** that could later breach the above requirements. Meeting all of these points ensures that VirtualQ can safely integrate the third‑party software without legal exposure, while still being able to deliver commercial value and maintain future flexibility.

Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

   The names give a clear indication of their purpose:

   - **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)** – an optimizer that automatically adjusts system parameters in a *flexible* (rule‑based or configuration‑driven) manner. It is used to continuously fine‑tune the virtualQ platform (e.g., routing, load‑balancing, resource allocation) without requiring manual re‑coding, allowing the system to adapt to varying workloads or client‑specific constraints.

   - **Automated Predictive Optimizer (APO)** – an optimizer that leverages *predictive* analytics / machine‑learning models to forecast future demand, usage patterns, or performance bottlenecks and then automatically applies the optimal configuration or resource plan. It goes beyond rule‑based tuning by anticipating upcoming conditions and proactively optimizing the system.

4. **Combine the information into a concise answer**

### Optimizers offered by virtualQ

| Optimizer | What it does |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Automated Flexible Optimizer (AFO)** | Automatically fine‑tunes virtualQ’s operation using flexible, rule‑based or configuration‑driven adjustments. It continuously adapts routing, load‑balancing, and other runtime parameters to meet current workload and client‑specific requirements without manual intervention. |

expected_answer: VirtualQ provides a range of optimizers which are algorithms used to calculate caller waiting times in its intelligent callback system. Each optimizer fits different levels of data availability and customer goals. The Flexible Optimizer adapts to partial real time data while the Dynamic Optimizer relies on live ACD data to adjust callbacks instantly. The Predictive Optimizer uses machine learning with historical and real time inputs to forecast wait times and schedule callbacks proactively. The proprietary virtualQ Algorithm offers a general solution when deeper integrations are not possible and the Static Optimizer uses fixed rules for environments with little or no real time data. Automated variants such as the Automated Flexible Optimizer and Automated Predictive Optimizer further reduce manual setup and improve adaptation over time. Together these options let virtualQ support customers across a wide range of integration depths and data richness.

Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response:
1. **Relevant Information from the Context:**
   - The use of third-party software and services must avoid legal issues.
   - Special attention is given to data privacy due to compliance with the EU’s GDPR.
   - Data privacy agreements are critical, especially for services run by third-party providers, as these may need to be included in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) between virtualQ and its clients.
   - The geographic location of services is a consideration—likely because data transfers outside the EU may violate GDPR.
   - Licenses and intellectual property (IP) ownership are evaluated, particularly for open-source components.
   - Not all open-source licenses are suitable—only "appropriate" ones are acceptable, where “appropriate” means:
     - Usable in a commercial setting.
     - Can be sold along with the virtualQ system in an exit scenario (e.g., acquisition or licensing).
   - Certain customers (e.g., those under SGB or KRITIS regulations) have even stricter privacy and security requirements than standard GDPR or Federal Office of IT Security (BSI) standards.

2. **How These Pieces Connect:**
   - Legal compliance is driven by data sensitivity and regulatory scope (GDPR, SGB, KRITIS).
   - The use of third-party tools affects not only internal operations but also contractual obligations with clients, particularly through DPAs.
   - Licensing determines whether virtualQ can legally integrate, use, and potentially resell the software.
   - Legal risk is heightened if third parties could access regulated data—so even theoretical access must be assessed.
   - The evaluation of licenses ties into long-term business scenarios like commercialization or exit strategies.

3. **Conclusion:**
   The legal criteria for third-party software and services include:
   - Compliance with GDPR and other applicable regulations (e.g., SGB, KRITIS).
   - Data processing capabilities that allow inclusion in DPAs with clients.
   - Data privacy agreements and restrictions on data access, including jurisdictional controls based on geo-location of services.
   - Use of licenses that permit commercial use and redistribution, especially in an exit scenario.
   - Proper evaluation of IP ownership and open-source license compatibility.

**Final Answer:**
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include: (1) GDPR compliance and adherence to stricter regulations like SGB and KRITIS; (2) the ability to include the service in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with clients; (3) data privacy protections, including restrictions on data access and appropriate geo-location of services; (4) use of commercially permissible licenses that allow integration and resale of the virtualQ system; and (5) clear intellectual property rights and compatibility with open-source licenses in commercial and exit scenarios.

1. **Relevant Information from the Context:**

- **Internal Audits & Design Verification** are conducted by internal teams. These include:
  - Architecture and design sessions within the team.
  - Reviews during pull request processes for smaller decisions.
